validity.recommendation: No action — existence, classification and non-duplicate status are all solidly confirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed, independent of GEM/wiki. Southern Natural Gas (SNG) is a real, FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission system, wholly-owned 50/50 by subsidiaries of Kinder Morgan and Southern Company, HQ'd in Birmingham AL, in continuous service since the late 1920s. Confirmed via: (1) Kinder Morgan's own live current system page (kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/SNG) describing SNG's ownership, route and services today; (2) Kinder Morgan's South System Expansion 4 (SSE4) FAQ PDF dated 11 Aug 2025, an active FERC pre-filing project (Docket opened 30 Oct 2024) on this same system; (3) the 2016 PR Newswire release announcing the Southern Company/Kinder Morgan strategic venture; (4) Southern Company's own 2016 transaction factsheet PDF; (5) UtilityDive's independent 2016 trade-press coverage of the same transaction closing; (6) a Wikipedia stub (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Natural_Pipeline) that carries its own citation to an archived FERC pipeline-code page (not GEM). CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as gas transmission — every source describes SNG as a large interstate natural-gas transmission trunk system, not a gathering/processing/NGL line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 45-row TX-operating roster provided — no other row describes this LA/MS/AL-to-Southeast trunk corridor; SNG is a distinct, unique physical system (its Georgia interconnects to Elba Express / Carolina Gas Transmission are separate GEM entities outside this roster, not roster duplicates). HARVESTED-POOL COVERAGE: opened all 3 of this row's harvested wiki citations — the bit.ly link resolved (301) to the Wikipedia stub above and was read; the PR Newswire article was read in full; the Southern Company factsheet PDF was downloaded and read via `pdftotext -layout` after url_verifier gave a false-negative content match on it (a known PDF-layout extraction limitation per the verifier's own docstring — manually confirmed the exact expected text is present in the extracted layout). Supplemented with independent open-web research: Kinder Morgan's current SNG page, its Aug-2025 SSE4 FAQ PDF (same pdftotext-manual-verify false-negative pattern, likely from the document's 'ti'-ligature encoding), and UtilityDive (blocked by the verifier's bot-wall UA — 403 — but confirmed live and content-matching manually via curl with a real browser User-Agent, another documented false-negative class).

validity.recommendation: Verify StartState/Province=Texas — check whether SNG still has any Texas-side interconnect/origin, or correct the start state to Louisiana per the operator's current description.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartState/Province=Texas, EndState/Province=Florida. EndState=Florida is well corroborated: Florida is named as an SNG market state by Kinder Morgan's current page, the 2016 PR Newswire release, and UtilityDive's independent 2016 coverage (3 agreeing sources). StartState=Texas is NOT corroborated by the CURRENT operator description: Kinder Morgan's own live SNG page states the system 'extend[s] from natural gas supply basins in Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama' — Texas is absent from both the current supply-basin list and the current market-area list for SNG specifically (checked the full page text; Texas appears only in the descriptions of KM's other, separate Texas intrastate systems on the same page — HPL, Tejas, KMTP, etc. — never in the SNG paragraph). By contrast, the 2016 PR Newswire release and UtilityDive's 2016 article both DID call Texas one of SNG's supply-basin states at the time of the Kinder Morgan/Southern Company transaction. This is either a genuine change in the system's footprint since 2016 (an interconnect or lateral divested/retired) or looser regional language in the 2016 PR materials — either way, the current authoritative operator source does not support Texas as an origin state today, so this warrants a human check before continuing to carry Texas as the StartState.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile LengthKnown (12,231 km / 7,600 mi) against Kinder Morgan's current stated ~6,900-mile (~11,105 km) system length.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown=12,231.00 km converts to exactly 7,600.4 miles — matching the 2016 PR Newswire release's '7,600-mile pipeline system' figure to one decimal (12,231 = 7,600 x 1.60934), and roughly matching Southern Company's own 2016 factsheet ('7,000-mile') and UtilityDive's independent 2016 reporting ('approximately 7,000 miles'). So the value is genuinely traceable to real, contemporaneous, non-GEM sources from the 2016 KM/Southern Company transaction. HOWEVER, Kinder Morgan's CURRENT live SNG system page (accessed today) states the system is 'an approximately 6,900-mile pipeline system' — about 700 miles (~9%) shorter than GEM's figure, and this is the operator's own present-day characterization, not a decade-old press figure. Flagging as a material spec conflict per the sweep's spec rule rather than silently keeping the 2016-vintage number: either the system's mapped mileage has genuinely changed since 2016 (divestiture/rationalization) or GEM's figure needs revisiting against the current operator disclosure.

validity.recommendation: Verify Capacity (3,900 MMcf/d) against Kinder Morgan's current stated ~4.4 Bcf/d design capacity; no source found supporting the 3,900 figure specifically.
validity.researcher_notes: No independent source was found that states SNG's design capacity as 3,900 MMcf/d specifically — this value could not be corroborated. Kinder Morgan's own South System Expansion 4 (SSE4) Project FAQ, dated 11 Aug 2025 (an active FERC pre-filing docket opened 30 Oct 2024, so this is a current, authoritative operator disclosure, not a stale figure): 'SNG has a design capacity of approximately 4.4 billion cubic feet [per day].' SSE4 itself is described as adding a further ~1.3 Bcf/d on top of that existing 4.4 Bcf/d baseline, and has not yet gone into service (still in FERC pre-filing as of the FAQ's date), so the 4.4 Bcf/d figure is the PRE-expansion current capacity, not a future/planned number. GEM's 3,900 MMcf/d (3.9 Bcf/d) is materially lower than this current baseline. GEM's LastUpdated for this row is 2023-08-30, so it is possible 3,900 was accurate for 2023 and capacity has grown since via other completed expansions (e.g., the search-surfaced 'Evangeline Pass Phase 2' project, ~1.1 Bcf/d, completed 'in May' of an unconfirmed year) — but that would need to be checked against dated FERC/company records rather than assumed. Not filling a replacement number since I could not independently verify 4.4 Bcf/d beyond this single (albeit authoritative and current) operator source.
